articles.title: Google presenta teclado para escribir con una mano: sus botones se desplazan sobre una cinta transportadora
articles.summary:
La división japonesa de Google presentó un teclado experimental que invierte la lógica tradicional de escritura: en lugar de que el usuario mueva los dedos hacia las teclas, son las teclas las que se desplazan hacia el dedo. El dispositivo, bautizado Gboard Conveyor Belt Version, monta sus botones sobre cuatro cintas transportadoras que giran en bucle hasta que el carácter deseado llega frente al usuario.
El nombre original en japonés, Gboard kurukuru version, hace referencia a la palabra kuru, que se traduce aproximadamente como “acercarse o llegar”, y alude al movimiento circular y repetitivo de las cintas. El equipo de Gboard explicó que la idea parte de una observación simple: los teclados convencionales están diseñados para dos manos, por lo que escribir con una sola mano o un solo dedo obliga a desplazar todo el brazo y la palma por la superficie del dispositivo.
Cuatro cintas con 29 teclas cada una
El diseño distribuye 116 teclas en total, repartidas en cuatro bandas con 29 caracteres cada una. El usuario presiona el carácter en el momento exacto en que pasa frente a su dedo. A diferencia de los teclados tradicionales, las mayúsculas y minúsculas tienen botones separados, sin necesidad de recurrir a la tecla Shift, una decisión que la compañía considera más intuitiva para este formato.
Según la publicación de la empresa, el dispositivo está pensado para la escritura con una sola mano, por ejemplo mientras se toma una taza de té o se maneja un mouse con la otra. También…

Developer Experience as a Business Strategy: Lessons from the New DevEx Report
Ana Jiménez Santamaría | 10 October 2026
A broad look at developer experience research reveals a gap. Designing with Dev-X: A Systematic Mapping of Developer Experience Interventions and Their Business Impact, brings together more than a hundred empirical studies. Only 39 of those studies explicitly connected DevEx interventions to outcomes and organizational KPIs.
This finding stood out to me. Through my work with developer and open source communities, I’ve become interested in how understanding developers’ needs can inform an organization’s strategy. This research points to an area worth exploring further: connecting improvements in their everyday experience to the outcomes the organization wants to achieve.
The new Linux Foundation Research report, Optimizing Developer Experience for High Engineering Performance, offers a practical framework for approaching this challenge. Written by Ibrahim Haddad, with a foreword by Arun Gupta (NVIDIA), and published with the Developer Relations Foundation, it helps organizations make developer experience part of how they prioritize investment, organize work, and measure progress.
The report focuses on engineering teams within organizations, with lessons that can help us think about supporting developers who use our products and services.

articles.title: « Votre compte Telegram n’est plus seulement le vôtre » : une faille de Telegram Desktop permettait de voler un compte en un clic
articles.summary:
Telegram a corrigé la faille en septembre sans en dire un mot.
Le 7 octobre 2026, le chercheur BeakSec a publié la version finale d’une chaîne d’attaque visant Telegram Desktop, l’application bureau de la messagerie privée.
Vu du côté de la victime, le scénario se résumait à peu de chose, puisqu’il suffisait d’être ajouté à un groupe par un inconnu puis de cliquer sur un lien posté dans la conversation.
« Vous cliquez dessus, et votre compte Telegram n’est plus seulement le vôtre », écrit l’expert en ouverture de son billet. Référencée CVE-2026-107181 et notée 8,6 sur 10, la faille touchait toutes les versions jusqu’à la 7.2.8 et a été confirmée sur Windows.
Un point-virgule mal géré
Tâchons de décortiquer le problème. Ici, la faille reposait sur une confusion entre une donnée et une commande. Lorsqu’un lien « tg:// » est ouvert depuis le navigateur, Telegram Desktop transmet ce lien à l’application déjà ouverte via un canal local entre processus.
Ce lien est converti en texte sous la forme « OPEN:<url>; » : le préfixe OPEN: indique à Telegram qu’il doit ouvrir l’adresse qui suit, et le point-virgule marque la fin de l’instruction.
Problème, Telegram ne protégeait pas les points-virgules pouvant figurer dans l’URL elle-même. Ainsi, un attaquant pouvait en ajouter dans le lien : le processus qui envoie le message estimait que ce n’était qu’un simple caractère de l’adresse tandis que pour l’application qui le reçoit, c’était la fin d’une instruction et le début d’une autre.

Selbst wenn die KI-Blase platzt: Warum Speicherchips auf Jahre Mangelware bleiben

Und auch bei Smartphones, Motherboards und Co. ziehen die Preise stetig an, weil die Herstellungskosten steigen. articles.summary:
A Kansas City, Missouri man has been sentenced to 32 months in jail for crimes related to a ransom attack against his own company.
The DOJ has announced the sentencing of Daniel Rhyne. He had already pleaded guilty to ‘extortion in relation to a threat to cause damage to a protected computer’ and ‘intentional damage to a protected computer’.
Fifty-nine-year-old Rhyne had been a core infrastructure engineer at an industrial firm headquartered in Somerset County, New Jersey. The firm provides services to industries involved in aquaculture, biopharmaceuticals, chemistry, electronics, food and beverage, healthcare, hydrogen mobility, manufacturing and industrial processing, metals, oil and gas, and pulp and paper.
In November 2023, Rhyne placed scheduled tasks on the firm’s domain controller that would delete 13 domain administrator accounts; change passwords to 301 domain user accounts; change passwords to two local administrator accounts that would impact 254 servers; and change passwords to two local administrator accounts impacting 3,284 workstations. The effect was to deny the firm access to its systems and data.
Where passwords were changed, it was generally to ‘TheFr0zenCrew!’.
The scheduled tasks were completed late afternoon on November 25. Within an hour, certain employees received an e-mail from an external address. articles.title: What is umami?
articles.summary:
Characterised at the beginning of the 20th century in Japan, umami literally means “delicious taste” or “tasty taste”. Umami flavour was accepted as one of the five basic tastes at the beginning of the 2000s, on the basis of its detection by the taste receptors present within the patches of tissue or papillae on our tongue. Umami’s distinctive, savoury flavour is mainly produced by certain amino acids that make up proteins, including glutamic acid or its salt form, glutamate (sodium).
Umami has a unique characteristic: a phenomenon of synergy. This means that the flavour of glutamate is drastically increased by certain compounds found in certain foods or ingredients such as bonito – a cousin of tuna – dried (katsuobushi) or yeast extracts.
A mysterious flavour in the West
Although many molecules can produce the umami taste, it is one of the most little known and difficult sensations to describe, mainly because of the rarity of compounds that possess a pure umami taste.
The umami taste can however be generated among foods that are far more widespread than you would imagine: this is the case for algae (kombu algae), mushrooms (shiitake, truffle…) and also as has long been the case with basic kitchen staples like cheese (Parmesan, mature Comté, for example), cured meats (salami, dried ham…), fresh fish (especially bonito, salmon), seafood (shrimp, crabs, scallops…) or simply… tomato juice.

articles.title: 730 millions de données volées : la police fait tomber Reacher, le moteur de recherche pirate de 3 ados
articles.summary:
Un nouveau site pirate vient de tomber en France. Ce mardi 6 octobre, l’Office anti-cybercriminalité (OFAC) a interpellé trois administrateurs présumés de Reacher, qui a été rebaptisé Stryx au début de l’été. Pour rappel, un lookup est un moteur de recherche qui recense et revend des données personnelles issues de fuites et de piratages.
Trois mineurs de 17 ans à l’origine du site
Les trois suspects sont des mineurs de 17 ans, jusqu’ici inconnus de la justice. Ils sont soupçonnés de recel d’extraction frauduleuse de données, de détention et de transmission frauduleuse de données, en bande organisée. Ils encourent jusqu’à dix ans de prison. Leur procès est prévu en janvier 2027. Notez que ce n’est pas la première fois que de très jeunes pirates se retrouvent dans le viseur des autorités françaises. En juin, la France avait déjà arrêté sept jeunes hackers après plus de 1 500 cyberattaques perpétrées sur le territoire.
Créé en mars 2026, Stryx revendiquait 730 millions de lignes de données indexées, et affichait plus de 3 millions de requêtes. On tapait une information quelconque et le site renvoyait tout ce qu’il savait sur la personne. Il suffisait d’un nom, d’un numéro de téléphone, d’un IBAN ou même d’une plaque d’immatriculation. L’accès était gratuit ou sur abonnement, et les utilisateurs pouvaient acheter des crédits supplémentaires pour faire plus de recherches.
L’enquête a été ouverte le 15 mai, après un signalement de l’association e-Enfance. Dans la foulée de l’opérat…

articles.title: Anthropic is cutting off its internal evaluations from the internet
articles.summary:
After a recent spate of high-profile incidents in which AI agents escaped containment, Anthropic is cutting off internet access for all internal evaluations. In a report Friday, the company detailed “unintended model actions,” including submitting a false tip regarding an unsolved murder, that led to the decision.
Anthropic is cutting off its internal evaluations from the internet
Anthropic is is keeping its agents offline during testing until it can prevent ‘unintended model actions.’
Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal and we had already turned off live internet access for some high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations, we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures (described in the remediation section of this post) reliably catch behaviors like these.
The ability to gain access to the live internet, even when models were supposed to be operating in isolation, has been an ongoing issue for AI companies. Many incidents, including the Hugging Face attack, involved agents that were supposed to be denied access to the internet. Yet, in case after case, the agents found creative solutions to bypass those restrictions. Physically removing internet access would certainly improve security around AI testing, but it would also limit its usefulness.
The report also amounts to an admission that Anthropic is often unaware of what its agents are doing and does not have a reliable s…

articles.title: Depuis que j’ai appris ce que signifie PPS sur un chargeur, je ne branche mon téléphone que s’il en est équipé
articles.summary:
Depuis que j’ai appris ce que signifie PPS sur un chargeur, je ne branche mon téléphone que s’il en est équipé
Depuis que les fabricants ne glissent plus de chargeur dans la boîte, il faut l'acheter à part. Et là, tous les blocs ne se valent pas. Derrière l'USB-C universel se cache un détail décisif, la technologie PPS, qui ajuste la charge en temps réel pour préserver la batterie. Choisir le bon adaptateur n'est plus un luxe, c'est un geste de bon sens.
Vous déballez votre nouveau smartphone, vous soulevez le carton, et vous cherchez. En vain. Le petit bloc blanc qui accompagnait chaque téléphone a disparu, remplacé par un simple câble. Face au mur de chargeurs du magasin, tous estampillés USB-C à des prix allant du simple au décuple, une question se pose, que peu savent trancher : lequel choisir vraiment, et surtout, à quoi bon payer plus cher ?
Le port est universel, pas la charge
Depuis fin 2024, une directive européenne impose l'USB-C à tous les smartphones neufs, mettant fin à la jungle des connecteurs propriétaires. Conjuguée à la volonté des fabricants de réduire leurs coûts et leurs déchets, cette règle a un effet de bord : le bloc secteur a quitté la boîte. Le connecteur est donc le même pour tous. Mais c'est là que s'arrête l'uniformité. Car brancher une prise identique ne garantit pas la même charge.
Tout se joue dans le dialogue invisible entre le chargeur et le téléphone. Le standard qui régit cet échange s'appelle l'USB Power Delivery, ou USB-PD, aujourd'hui ca…

Sur Terre, les nuages prennent des formes très variées, qui laissent libre cours à l’imagination. Mais sur Mars, ces phénomènes sont plus rares et encore mal compris. Si plusieurs phénomènes nuageux ont déjà été repérés et étudiés, il y en a un qui sort du lot et qui fait l’objet d’une étude parue ce mercredi 7 octobre dans la revue Nature Geoscience.
Ce nuage a été surnommé AMEC, pour Arsia Mons Elongated Clouds. Il se forme sous le vent d’Arsia Mons, un volcan de 20 kilomètres de haut (plus du double de l’Everest), et peut s’étirer sur 1 800 kilomètres, soit près de deux fois la longueur du Royaume-Uni. Plus étonnant encore, le nuage suit un cycle régulier. Il apparaît le matin, s’évapore dans la journée et revient le lendemain, et ce pendant plusieurs mois, à chaque printemps et été de l’hémisphère sud martien.
Expliquer avec de la « physique exotique »
AMEC a été repéré pour la première fois en 2018 par la sonde européenne Mars Express. Les chercheurs l’ont ensuite retrouvé sur des images d’archives plus anciennes, jusque sur des clichés de la sonde Viking 2 de la NASA, dans les années 1970. Sa découverte a lancé plusieurs études sur son fonctionnement. Ces travaux ont établi qu’il s’agit d’un nuage orographique, un type de nuage qu’on observe aussi sur Terre et qui se forme quand le vent bute sur un relief, ici le volcan Arsia Mons. Mais jusqu’ici, aucune simulation ne parvenait à reproduire le nuage tel qu’il apparaît sur les images.

articles.title: Ledger wallet tampering suspected after reports of crypto thefts
articles.summary:
Reports have been mounting that users of the Ledger crypto wallet have seen their accounts drained, and it appears to be related to tampered hardware sold by CryptoBillis. Ledger has asked CryptoBillis to pause all sales of its wallets while it conducts an investigation. Ledger has confirmed that “one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.”
Ledger wallet tampering suspected after reports of crypto thefts
A spy implant in some Ledger crypto wallets may be the root of an $86 million supply chain attack.
Photos and videos posted on X and Threads appear to show a small circuit board sandwiched under the screen. The implant allegedly intercepts anything displayed on the screen, including the seed passphrase shown during the initial setup. Using an embedded SIM card, the implant then sends that information back to the attacker, who can then siphon funds from user accounts.
Reports indicate that whoever is behind the hack has stolen over $86 million worth of crypto from hundreds of wallets. There’s no indication that Ledger’s systems have been compromised or that wallets purchased directly from the company have been affected. Instead, the issue appears to be a supply chain attack primarily involving users in Southeast Asia and the CryptoBillis reseller. Ledger has provided guidance on how to check if your wallet has been tampered with.
Update October 10th, 2026: Added additional statment from Ledger.

articles.title: Gaming consoles are more expensive than ever, and fewer people are buying them

Bottom line: The US console market is slowing, and more expensive hardware is making it harder to attract buyers. Consumers bought 559,000 consoles in August, down 15% from a year earlier and the lowest August total since 2013, according to figures shared by Circana's Mat Piscatella. The average selling price rose from $476 in 2025 to $541 in 2026.
For manufacturers, those higher prices can soften the financial impact of falling sales. Sony's PlayStation hardware revenue increased 17% year over year, even though unit sales declined 11%. Higher-tier models helped make up the difference.
But the figures also show the limits of mid-generation upgrades. More expensive machines allow manufacturers to generate additional revenue without necessarily expanding the audience for their hardware.
Console prices are at historical highs, driven by pressure on component costs and the introduction of premium models such as the $900 PS5 Pro. That leaves buyers facing a higher cost of entry than in previous console cycles.
The slowdown extends across all three major manufacturers. Xbox unit sales fell 31% year over year, reaching their lowest August level since 2020. Nintendo unit sales declined 15% from August 2025.
The average price a consumer has paid for a new Xbox console in 2026 YTD ending August is $529, 26% higher than a year ago, while the average PlayStation console has sold for $597, 20% higher than last year. Both prices are at all-time US highs. Price sensitivity is becoming a rea…

L’expédition a fait demi-tour après la mort tragique d’un de ses membres. Cette région reculée est connue sous le nom de bassin sous-glaciaire de Wilkes, une immense étendue de glace mesurant 1 400 kilomètres sur 400 kilomètres.
Or, une grande partie du bassin de Wilkes se trouve bien en dessous du niveau de la mer. Si toute la glace du bassin venait à fondre, cela ferait monter le niveau de la mer de trois à quatre mètres. Il est aussi probable que les torrents d’eau de fonte perturberaient des courants océaniques à la base de la circulation océanique, et provoqueraient des bouleversements majeurs pour la vie marine et le climat plus généralement.

The actor targeted multiple Korean banks, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, and Hana Bank, exposing clients ' personal data and credit card information, and causing system outages in some cases.
The South Korean government reacted with an emergency meeting and calls for immediate security measures for critical IT systems.
Security firm CrowdStrike confirmed the use of ARTEX AI, up until recently an open-source agentic penetration testing suite developed in China.
Researchers identified the attacker's infrastructure and found open directories with Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files, and Claude memory files.
“The ARTEX instance used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the primary LLM backend, and the threat actor supplemented this LLM with GLM-5.3 (Zhipu AI) and Grok 4.6 for additional Claude Code sessions,” CrowdStrike explained.
“The threat actor likely accessed DeepSeek via the likely LLM API proxy/reseller xcai[.]pro,” the researchers noted.
These records also provided insight into the attacker’s activities, with targets overlapping those named in previous reporting about financial-sector breaches, allowing for high-confidence linking.
Because the threat actor used the same AI tools to create a résumé, they also exposed identification, contact, and Telegram account details.

articles.title: Workers are now pretending to use AI to impress their bosses, survey says
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Believing in the massive productivity gains promised by artificial intelligence providers, many employers have pushed workers to use generative AI as much as possible. However, recent research suggests uncertainty is driving employees to exaggerate or fake their AI use to please their bosses. Above all, workers want clearer guidance on using the technology.
According to the findings, which come from research conducted in part by business intelligence firm Visier, nearly half of surveyed US employees misreport how much they use generative AI in the workplace.
In a trend the company calls "Performative AI," 48% of 1,000 surveyed full-time US employees said they exaggerated their AI usage or expertise to coworkers or bosses. The main reason is that workers want to appear experienced with AI tools but don't get enough training or guidance on them. Almost half of those surveyed, around 45%, say they feel pressured to use AI but aren't confident they can do so effectively.
Uncertainty surrounding AI tools and employers' plans for the technology is the main theme in Visier's results. Many employees say their leaders don't fully understand AI's capabilities or how it truly affects the workplace.

articles.title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
articles.summary:
In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft’s CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice and actions we simply accept or reject. He calls for building a more transparent system where models can be contained, observed, and leaves behind “tamper-proof human readable evidence.”
Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
Microsoft’s CEO calls for putting an ‘emergency brake’ on AI.
Many of his recommendations align with what we’ve heard from others in the industry: timely incident disclosure, independent audits, verifiable data, and containment. It’s on that last point that he appears to go slightly farther than some others in the field, saying:
We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start. Think of it like an emergency brake. An authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task. More advanced models will require more advanced containment technologies that we need to standardize on.
Unfortunately, Nadella also refers to AI as “super intelligence” throughout the post.

No dijo nadie nunca, salvo quizás los arándanos: un estudio de la Universidad de Minnesota ha descubierto el efecto de los lobos (de su ingesta) sobre la germinación de los arándanos. Concretamente, aquellas semillas que se habían comido los lobos germinaron en un 96 % frente al 69% de las que no. articles.title: AnyPS5 project reaches critical GPU milestone in race to enable running PS5 games natively on PC — 100% shader instruction coverage is a massive step forward, but playing all PS5 games natively on PC is still far off
articles.summary:
AnyPS5 project reaches critical GPU milestone in race to enable running PS5 games natively on PC — 100% shader instruction coverage is a massive step forward, but playing all PS5 games natively on PC is still far off
The new project is not an emulator, but an attempt to get PS5 games running natively on PC.
The open-source AnyPS5 project has reached 100% GPU shader instruction coverage, a significant milestone in its effort to run PlayStation 5 games natively on Windows and Linux PCs. The project's live progress tracker now lists all 1,166 instructions in its tracked AMD RDNA 1 and RDNA 2 instruction set as implemented. There's a fairly important asterisk attached to that number, though: it doesn't mean the PS5's GPU is fully supported, much less that PS5 games are ready to run on your PC.
The distinction is in how AnyPS5 defines "implemented." In this case, it means the project's shader decoder recognizes an instruction. That's an essential first step, but it doesn't necessarily mean every instruction is implemented in translation to SPIR-V, never mind a guarantee that the instruction's behavior is correct in every situation, that every GPU feature is supported, or that a game's shaders will render properly. Consider the network libraries: libSceHttp is reported at 95% implementation, but the technical-debt document explicitly states that no HTTP request reaches the network in the current implementation.

Jev se presentó el 15 de septiembre de 2026 y, según la empresa, se volvió viral de forma casi inmediata. TypeSafe afirma que un tercio de las compañías de la lista Fortune 500 ya lo utiliza, aunque no identificó cuáles.
Qué hace este modelo de inteligencia artificial
A diferencia de los modelos de lenguaje que dominan el mercado desde hace cuatro años, Jev está construido sobre una arquitectura de transformadores pero no genera texto.
El sistema produce lo que la compañía llama decisiones calibradas: probabilidades pensadas para que el software tome acciones automáticas, no para redactar respuestas o código.

Anthropic’s new OSS Scanner, launched last week as part of its broader Cyber Mission, exposes a problem inside the company’s security research operation. Claude is finding potential vulnerabilities faster than human researchers can verify them.
Over six months of scanning some of the world’s most widely used open source projects, Anthropic’s models surfaced more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities. Its human review pipeline, which relies on six external security research firms to reproduce and triage findings, has worked through only about 6,000.
A disclosure dashboard puts some numbers behind the problem. As of October 2, outside security firms had confirmed 5,674 of the 6,123 findings they reviewed as valid, but only 516 vulnerabilities had been patched upstream.
The company sent 6,157 findings to maintainers, and 584 CVE and GitHub Security Advisory identifiers were issued, though some findings received both. Roughly 23,000 candidates remain unreviewed.
Claude is finding potential vulnerabilities faster than human researchers can verify them.
How the fast track works
Instead of making maintainers wait for its researchers to work through the backlog, Anthropic is giving eligible projects free, periodic scans powered by its top models, including Claude Mythos. The findings go directly to maintainers, without anyone at Anthropic validating them first.

But it's not just games. Open-source clones of Adobe apps showed up on GitHub almost overnight. Earlier in the year, a single blog post about COBOL knocked IBM's stock off a cliff. These might look like separate stories, but they share one common thread: AI has sharply cut the cost of understanding old code, as long as something can check its work.
So yes, AI is a big part of it, but it's not the whole story. Three things converged.
TL;DR: why this is happening now
- Years of human groundwork were already in place
Many of today's headlines sit on decompilations volunteers spent five or six years building. AI is largely finishing the last stretch, the part where these projects historically stalled forever.
- Matching decompilation suits AI agents unusually well. 
Matching decompilation means rebuilding source code that compiles byte-for-byte identical to the original binary. That gives an AI agent a pass/fail check it can run over and over without a human grading its work. Coding agents can loop against that check for hours unattended, and the same trick works anywhere old and new outputs can be compared, from game code to bank batch jobs.

Valery was able to do this by running Pac-Man through the MAME arcade emulator and using ReShade to inject DLSS 5 into the graphics pipeline, and RenoDX to allow the DLSS 5 parameters to be tweaked. articles.title: Unos científicos dicen que llevábamos años calculando mal el polvo del hielo marciano. Y eso cambia lo que sabemos sobre su habitabilidad
articles.summary:
Aunque tenemos pruebas geológicas de que en algún momento del pasado fluyó agua líquida por Marte, hoy en día los únicos depósitos de agua que se han hallado en la superficie se encuentran en forma de hielo. Un hielo que, según los estudios publicados hasta ahora, debe tener un 25% de polvo. Este no es un dato trivial. La cantidad de polvo que hay en el hielo de un planeta puede decirnos muchas cosas sobre su habitabilidad. El problema es que, según un estudio publicado recientemente por científicos de la Universidad de Washington, ese dato estaba posiblemente sobreestimado. Más bien, parece que en el hielo del planeta rojo hay solo un 3% de polvo. Ahora bien, ¿qué tiene que ver eso con la presencia o ausencia de vida?
Un método inadecuado. Normalmente, los cálculos sobre la cantidad de polvo en el hielo marciano se realizaban mediante un método desarrollado a partir del regolito lunar. Se pensaba que el mismo método podría usarse para cualquier material en cualquier planeta. Sin embargo, cuando se probó para medir los niveles de polvo en el hielo de la Tierra, los datos eran incoherentes con la realidad.
Por eso, los autores de este nuevo estudio decidieron usar un método más específico, que sí resulta eficaz en el hielo terrestre. Cuando lo probaron con los datos espectrales del hielo marciano tomados por sondas como Mars Express o Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, encontraron que se había estado sobreestimando la cantidad de polvo. articles.title: Traqué depuis des mois, un cadre présumé du ransomware Qilin arrêté pendant ses vacances au Japon

Un Russe de 28 ans, soupçonné d'occuper un rôle important au sein du groupe de ransomware Qilin, a été arrêté au Japon puis extradé vers l'Allemagne. Une interpellation rendue possible par plusieurs mois d'infiltration policière.
Il pensait partir en vacances au Japon, mais son séjour a été écourté. En mai dernier, un ressortissant russe de 28 ans a été interpellé dans un hôtel d’Osaka, à la demande de la justice allemande. articles.title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has recently made Traces available in open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to the rest of the request path. Security rules, transformations, cache decisions, routing, Worker execution, and origin handling now appear as OpenTelemetry spans in a single request-level timeline, without any instrumentation to write. A pricing change arrives with it, and it applies to Workers Tracing too.
This fills a well-known gap for developers running distributed tracing through a proxy. Previously, the trace showed the client and then the application, with everything in between inferred from logs and configuration. Each supported step now arrives as a span with its timing, outcome, and attributes.
The questions Cloudflare uses as examples are the ones developers actually open tickets about. Which security rule blocked the request, and how long did rule evaluation take? Did a Transform Rule rewrite the URL before the application received it, and where did that happen relative to routing? Which Page Rule, Snippet, or Worker handled the request, and which route pattern matched? And where did the time go: one example shows a cache miss where 527ms of a 539ms request went to getting a response from the origin.
Nested cache, upstream, and origin spans showing where a request spent its time (Source: Cloudflare blog post)

Um einen möglichst griffigen Namen für ihr Projekt zu finden, müssen Forscherinnen und Forscher bisweilen kreativ sein. Das jüngste Beispiel ist Albatross, das steht für „Airborne Lander with Buoyant AuToROtating Sailing Sensor“ und ist teilweise von Wasservögeln inspiriert.
Auch jenseits der Namensgebung ist das Projekt der Singapore University of Technology and Design innovativ: Das interdisziplinäre Team um Shane Kyi Hla Win hat nämlich einen Roboter entwickelt, der sich verschiedener Prinzipien aus dem Tier- und Pflanzenreich bedient und mit vergleichsweise wenig Hardware gleich mehrere Funktionen erfüllt. Multimodale Robotik für Luft und Wasser

‘There's nothing that we can do’
Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes has said he believes there is no immediate need to slow down development of AI, despite several recent high-profile incidents leading to growing calls for such action.
Speaking to media at the recent Atlassian Team Europe 2026 event, Cannon-Brookes indicated that the company isn't planning any changes to its development lifecycle going forward.
"We tend to take a very textured approach to all that sort of thing," he noted. "Will we slow down? No, we won't. There's no logical world where I think that happens."
AI rewards
Cannon-Brookes went on to note that if nations are competing to stay ahead when it comes to the latest advances in the AI space, this will necessarily mean that development will continue at a pace.
"I think we're pretty good at broadly adapting to all these sorts of things," he said, looking to emphasize the rewards of AI, such as improved efficiency and productivity.
"Should we slow down? Should we pace the frontier? Should we not? It's out of our hands anyway. There's nothing that we can do."
"I think the reality of the global geopolitical world is not going to change. So we work out what we do about that world rather than wishing it was different. I don't know. Maybe I'm too pragmatic about it, but it's not in my control."

articles.title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge

AWS recently announced enhanced custom event buses for Amazon EventBridge, allowing organizations to share a centralized bus across accounts with ordered delivery, simplified subscriber management, event replay, content-based deduplication, and a new publisher/subscriber-based pricing model.
EventBridge is a managed event bus service for routing events between distributed applications and AWS services. As adoption grows across multi-account environments, teams often need multiple interconnected event buses, increasing routing costs and operational complexity while making event subscriptions harder to manage and features such as ordering more difficult to implement. Micah Walter, senior solutions architect at AWS, writes:
This workaround reintroduces the operational complexity that serverless architectures are meant to eliminate. Platform teams lose visibility into who is subscribing to which events, cross-account and bus-to-bus routing charges compound quickly, and teams that need capabilities like event ordering are forced to build complex workarounds or adopt entirely different technologies.
The enhanced EventBridge custom event bus provides a shared, organization-wide bus with cross-account publishing and subscriptions, ordered delivery, event replay, content-based deduplication, JSONata-based event transformation, and support for Avro and Protobuf payloads.

articles.title: Mucho antes de Manhattan, África levantó hace 2.800 años una estructura que las matemáticas definen como rascacielos
articles.summary:
Cuando pensamos en rascacielos, es culturalmente inevitable asociarlos al Nueva York y Chicago de finales del siglo XIX y principios del XX con toda la razón del mundo, pero puede que existieran antes, muchísimo antes. Vamos, casi 3000 años antes y en un sitio a priori bastante insospechado, o esa es la conclusión a la que acaba de llegar un estudio realizado en Etiopía.
¿El primer rascacielos africano? Allá por el año 800 a. C., en Yeha, en la región de Tigray en el norte del mencionado país africano se levantó un palacio llamado Grat Be'al Gibri. Hoy está en ruinas, reducido a parte de la planta baja y poco más, como puedes ver en la imagen que ilustra este artículo. Tenía una planta de 60 metros de ancho por 60 metros de ancho y por aquel entonces, era el mayor edificio de este tipo conocido en el sur de Arabia y África oriental de la época
La pregunta del millón es: ¿qué altura tenía el templo? Un equipo multidisciplinar alemán se propuso resolver esa pregunta, así que se pusieron manos a la obra. La respuesta: en el peor de los casos, entre 16 y 19. Ojo, eso no quiere decir que las tuviera, solo que sus muros serían capaces de soportarlas.
Por qué importa. Hasta ahora, la altura de este tipo de edificios derruidos se deducía a partir de textos y pinturas, porque no había un análisis estructural que diera más pistas. articles.title: 20 000 serveurs VPN contre 1 000, faut-il vraiment choisir le plus gros réseau ?

Des dizaines de milliers de serveurs chez l’un, vingt fois moins chez l’autre. À première vue, le choix semble vite fait. Pourtant, compter les serveurs d’un VPN ne dit pas combien d’utilisateurs ils accueillent, comment ils sont répartis ni ce que votre connexion peut en attendre.
Ce sont des chiffres qui prennent bien vite toute la place. Certains fournisseurs VPN revendiquent plusieurs dizaines de milliers de serveurs, quand d’autres exploitent des réseaux bien plus modestes. Face à de tels écarts, difficile de ne pas imaginer le mieux doté offrir davantage de vitesse, de stabilité et de possibilités de connexion. Et il est vrai qu’une infrastructure étendue présente de sérieux avantages. Sauf que le nombre de serveurs est avant tout une donnée d’inventaire, pas un résultat de test. Et pour comparer deux inventaires, il faut déjà savoir ce qu’ils recouvrent.
Des milliers de serveurs VPN, qu’est-ce qu’on compte au juste ?
Lorsqu’un fournisseur annonce disposer de plusieurs milliers de serveurs, on imagine assez naturellement autant de machines alignées dans des centres de données aux quatre coins du monde. Ce n’est pas nécessairement faux, mais le terme de serveur ne désigne pas toujours un équipement physique distinct.
Un serveur VPN reçoit les données circulant dans le tunnel chiffré depuis votre appareil, les déchiffre pour les acheminer vers leur destination, puis chiffre les données de retour avant de vous les renvoyer. Ce rôle peut être assuré par une machine physique…

articles.title: ‘La otra madre’ es una de las decepciones del año: terror insípido y sin mucho que ofrecer

La otra madre bien podría ser un remake de la icónica Coraline de Henry Selick. De hecho, ambas cintas comparten la misma idea de una familia que termina convirtiéndote en objeto de horrores. Pero mientras el clásico del stop motion logra profundizar en el tema con habilidad y volverlo impredecible, la versión de Rob Savage falla. Y lo hace, porque esta adaptación de Incidents Around the House de Josh Malerman carece de profundidad y habilidad para indagar en el miedo. Pero más complicado todavía, pierde demasiado tiempo en clichés, giros con poca imaginación y una pobre puesta en escena.
Más complejo todavía. La otra madre carece de la densidad de una historia en que se ponen a prueba (y más de una vez) todos los conceptos habituales sobre la maternidad. En realidad, varios de los puntos más interesantes de la película son justamente cuando se hace menos acartonada y experimenta. Por lo que la historia de una niña que sabe que hay una presencia sobrenatural acechando a su alrededor se hace un vehículo para analizar el miedo y la desolación. Pero el guion de Nathan Elston se vuelve progresivamente más plano al intentar aterrorizar con su colección de sobresaltos y jumpscares. Eso mientras la verdadera densidad de la historia queda relegada a un segundo plano.

articles.title: Dormir 80 minutos menos durante seis semanas nos hace engordar, según un nuevo estudio

Dormir entre 7 y 8 horas es importante. Aunque no todos lo hagamos, es algo que tenemos bastante asumido. Aun así, no dejan de sorprendernos las nuevas consecuencias que se van descubriendo que podría acarrear descansar durante menos tiempo. Por ejemplo, según un estudio reciente, dormir poco podría hacernos engordar, con todo lo que eso conlleva.
Solo seis semanas. En este estudio participaron 95 personas con riesgo cardiometabólico elevado, que aseguraron dormir normalmente más de 7 horas. Durante seis semanas, algunos tuvieron que acostarse 90 minutos más tarde. Equivaldría más o menos a 80 minutos menos de sueño. Después, durante otras seis semanas, volvieron a su rutina de sueño habitual. Otros hicieron lo mismo, pero en orden inverso: primero el sueño adecuado y después el restringido. A lo largo de las 12 semanas que duró el estudio se analizaron tanto su sueño como su actividad mediante pulseras.
Además, se tomaron datos de su peso, la circunferencia de la cintura, la composición corporal y los niveles de hormonas asociadas al apetito. Al comparar todos estos datos, se vio que esas seis semanas fueron suficientes para alterar su peso.
Medio kilo. De media, los participantes ganaron una libra de peso, equivalente más o menos a medio kilo. Esto puede parecernos poco. Sin embargo, los autores del estudio recuerdan que solo se hizo un análisis de seis semanas. Si lo extrapolamos a un año entero, la ganancia de peso puede ser considerable. articles.title: La historia real de ‘El precio de la red’: quién es Frances Haugen y qué fue el caso The Facebook Files
articles.summary:
Acaba de llegar a los cines El precio de la red, la esperada secuela de La red social. La película de David Fincher estrenada en 2010 es sin duda uno de los grandes largometrajes de Hollywood de este siglo. La historia del nacimiento de Facebook y todo lo que había detrás con la figura de Mark Zuckerberg conquistó al público. Ahora, el mismo guionista, Aaron Sorkin, se hace cargo también de la dirección con otra etapa clave de la compañía.
Y es que lo que se nos cuenta en El precio de la red también se inspira en la historia real de Facebook. Pero, esta vez, el filme nos cuenta algo mucho más reciente. Concretamente nos lleva hasta los años 2019-2021. En esa etapa sucedió la pandemia del coronavirus. Pero también ocurrió un hecho sin precedentes que obligó a Zuckerberg a tomar medidas.
Y es que la historia real de El precio de la red no es otra que el caso The Facebook Files. Una enorme filtración que puso en jaque a la compañía y que, a la larga, ha provocado la crisis actual de las redes sociales. Todo provocado gracias a la valentía de una mujer, Frances Haugen.
Quién es Frances Haugen y qué son The Facebook Files
Frances Haugen es una mujer que en 2019 trabajaba dentro de Facebook. Ingeniera de datos, formaba parte del equipo de integridad cívica de la empresa. articles.title: Context Language Models: Self-Managing Context to Improve Performance and Reduce Compute Costs
articles.summary:
Researchers from Meta, MIT, and the University of Washington introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), a new approach that enables language models to manage and edit their own context rather than relying on predefined mechanisms for summarization, compression, and information retrieval, reporting substantial gains in both performance and computational efficiency.
The researchers implemented the mechanism allowing LLMs to manage their own context by treating it as a file that they can update with no restrictions. This approach offers an alternative to conventional context-management strategies used to prevent context from growing indefinitely, such as compaction, offloading, and retrieval. Each of these techniques has its own limitations. Summarization can discard critical details or introduce inaccuracies, compaction often uses a predefined set of rules, and external memory requires agents to decide what to bring back into the context.
A CLM can instead rewrite old messages, preserve important facts, remove irrelevant information, maintain progress notes, and learn its own context-management strategies. The researchers emphasize that LLMs can learn strategies that go beyond existing human-designed approaches, potentially surpassing "existing human priors".
By shifting context management from external harness control to intrinsic model behavior, CLMs naturally enable in-context learning and parametric learning for context management. We first show that users can steer context …

articles.title: En 1945, EEUU gastó una fortuna intentando crear un "superperro": 500 cachorros y 13 años después descubrieron el problema
articles.summary:
Estados Unidos puso en marcha tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial uno de los experimentos caninos más ambiciosos jamás realizados: más de 500 perros, 13 años de investigación y 632.000 dólares de la época, cerca de nueve millones actuales, para estudiar hasta dónde podía llevarles la genética. Detrás estaba la Fundación Rockefeller y una pregunta heredada de una época mucho más oscura: si se elegían los genes adecuados, ¿sería posible criar un perro extraordinariamente inteligente?
La escuela del perro perfecto. El proyecto arrancó en Maine a mediados de los años 40 y acabó siendo conocido como la School for Dogs. Los investigadores John Paul Scott y John Fuller dispusieron de unas instalaciones enormes, decenas de trabajadores y cinco razas (cocker spaniel, beagle, pastor de Shetland, basenji y fox terrier de pelo duro) cuyos cachorros podían seguir desde el nacimiento.
Registraban su primer sobresalto, sus juegos, cuándo empezaban a comer sólidos o a mover la cola y, desde las cinco semanas, los sometían a pruebas de inteligencia, aprendizaje, dominancia, personalidad y capacidad de entrenamiento
Una respuesta sobre los humanos. La magnitud del proyecto se entiende mejor por el momento histórico en que nació. El Holocausto había desacreditado la eugenesia y sus pretensiones de mejorar al ser humano mediante la selección genética, mientras algunas figuras influyentes seguían convencidas de que la herencia explicaba buena parte de la inteligencia y el comportamiento.

articles.title: Fuite de données : la Cnaf suspend un site d'urgence après un « incident de cybersécurité »

Une nouvelle fuite de données frappe les services publics français. Ce samedi 10 octobre, la Caisse nationale des allocations familiales (Cnaf) a confirmé un incident de cybersécurité sur Vacaf, la plateforme d’aide aux vacances des Caf. Dans son communiqué, l’organisme indique qu’une fuite concernant les données des bénéficiaires a été signalée « hier soir ». Par précaution, l’accès au site vacaf.org a été rapidement coupé pour éviter toute nouvelle violation d’informations. La plateforme Vacaf permet aux familles éligibles de financer des séjours ou des colonies de vacances pour leurs enfants. Hébergée par un prestataire externe, la plateforme est pilotée par la Caf de l’Hérault.
À lire aussi : Fuite de données – le plus grand CHU de France (et d’Europe) a été piraté
Plus d’un million de dossiers piratés ?
Selon les premières analyses réalisées par la Cnaf, les données bancaires et les mots de passe d’accès aux services en ligne des Caf n’ont pas été compromis. Cependant, la Cnaf ne détaille pas les données touchées. Une plainte doit être déposée « dans les prochaines heures », et l’ANSSI ainsi que la CNIL ont été informées de la situation. Bonne nouvelle, les prestations des allocataires continuent d’être versées normalement. Le système Vacaf est totalement séparé du système qui gère les versements. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.
While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.
Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
Caddy
Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check.
For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you.

articles.title: Terminator T-800 en la vida real: el video de un robot que deja en el suelo al humano en un combate de boxeo
articles.summary:
El creador de contenido resultó con una lesión en su mano después de que el robot lo golpeara en esa zona fuertemente. (X: frankie_lapenna)
Un creador de contenido se enfrentó a un robot humanoide de casi 1,83 metros de altura dentro de una jaula y terminó en el suelo tras recibir un golpe durante el combate. La pelea fue detenida después de que Frankie LaPenna sufriera una lesión en una mano.
El robot era el T800, una plataforma humanoide desarrollada por la empresa EngineAI.
Su apariencia y el formato del enfrentamiento remitieron a Terminator, aunque la máquina no tomó decisiones de combate de forma autónoma: un operador la controlaba a distancia con un visor de realidad virtual y mandos.
La organización REK (Robot Entertainment Kombat) presentó el evento como la primera pelea ampliamente difundida entre una persona y un robot humanoide de tamaño real. Sin embargo, no se conocieron protocolos de seguridad ni un informe público sobre la lesión de LaPenna.
Cómo fue el enfrentamiento
LaPenna comenzó el combate con varios golpes contra la estructura del T800, aparentemente para comprobar su resistencia. Durante esos primeros intercambios, el robot mantuvo el equilibrio y respondió a los movimientos dentro de la jaula.
Luego, el T800 lanzó un golpe o una patada al cuerpo del creador de contenido y lo derribó.
LaPenna no pudo continuar y la pelea se detuvo, aunque REK aseguró públicamente que el humano había ganado el combate.

articles.title: World Mental Health Day: Rest in the Age of AI
articles.summary:
World Mental Health Day: Rest in the Age of AI
On World Mental Health Day, Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar explains how AI, screen time and meditation affect creativity, mental wellbeing and human connection.
Some years ago, our attention span was 45 to 50 minutes. Today, it has reduced to just 47 seconds. There is a severe attention deficit today.
The increased use of screens has a big role to play in this. When we stare at a screen for too long, we blink less. That affects the freshness and creativity of our minds. People today have more experiences than their senses and minds can handle. They feel emotionally exhausted and inwardly lost.
The purpose of technology is to bring us comfort. If it becomes the cause of distress, its purpose is lost. Holding onto cell phones all day hurts the nervous system. But if you are free from stress, you will use technology for a good purpose.
AI can have three interpretations.
The first is the absence of intelligence. A lot of what comes on social media is fake and AI-driven. We have to move ahead in AI, but with awareness. We forget to recognise intelligence in nature, which is an absence of intelligence on our part.
The second is artificial intelligence. It can only reproduce what is already stored, not create something new. It challenges our intellect and creativity, and pushes us to do something original. articles.title: We tested gaming performance in 17-year-old Windows 7 against Windows 11 on a modern gaming PC — older operating system delivers advantages in some scenarios
articles.summary:
We tested gaming performance in 17-year-old Windows 7 against Windows 11 on a modern gaming PC — older operating system delivers advantages in some scenarios
Can an old OS beat a new modern rig?
After the rough reception of Windows Vista, Windows 7 launched in 2009 to largely positive reviews. Even 17 years later, it remains one of the most beloved versions of Windows ever released. But how does this nearly two-decade-old operating system hold up on modern hardware? We managed to install Windows 7 on a modern PC and put it to the test across eight DirectX 11 games and two DirectX 9 titles to see how its gaming performance compares to Windows 11 today. Surprisingly, Windows 7 still carves out many notable wins over its successor.
At launch, Windows 7 was very similar to Windows Vista in many respects. Vista had introduced significant changes under the hood compared to Windows XP, including technologies such as SuperFetch, ReadyBoost, ReadyDrive, new asynchronous APIs, and other I/O improvements. It also introduced native processor power management and various memory-management enhancements. On the visual side, Vista was the first version of Windows to feature Windows Aero, with its distinctive glass-like window borders.
Windows 7 retained many of these underlying technologies while addressing several of Vista’s biggest criticisms. One notable improvement was greater control over User Account Control (UAC), allowing users to adjust how frequently they received UAC prompts. In V…

articles.title: Philadelphia police say AI companies must 'take all appropriate steps necessary' to restrict their models after an agent sent a fake unsolved murder tip-off
articles.summary:
Anthropic's AI submitted a false tip-off about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police — and the cops say the rogue behavior is 'unacceptable'
The tip wasn't followed up on
- An Anthropic AI model sent an unsolved murder tip-off to Philadelphia police
- Anthropic took two weeks to discover what had happened
- The tip-off was delivered to a spam folder and wasn't followed up on
We've seen AI inventing fake facts and spewing out hiking plans that put people in danger, but the technology has now progressed to the level of sending false, unsolicited tip-offs to the police about unsolved murder cases.
An Anthropic AI model emailed the Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tip line on July 18, TechCrunch reports, having come across the PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com portal during a website interaction test and learning about the case.
As the email went to the PPD spam folder it wasn't followed up on, and it appears no one was aware of the incident until Anthropic found out what had happened on September 28. The company then contacted the cops on Wednesday, October 7.

According to Cloudflare’s Kenton Varda, Cloudflare will use this acquisition to improve its Workers programming model and platform, which allows customers to build and run software on Cloudflare’s network. (Varda is principal engineer for Cloudflare Workers.)
Deno — which was co-founded by Bert Belder and Node.js creator Ryan Dahl — recently launched celld, an open source implementation of Workers, which Varda wrote “delighted” the Cloudflare team. Varda argued that contrary to “a popular theory” that the company “made Cloudflare Workers work differently from other cloud platforms in order to create ‘lock-in,’” the company believes “being open source and giving people an escape hatch is good business.”
Dahl, meanwhile, wrote that his team is “joining Cloudflare to make the Workers programming model a mainstream way to build servers.”
The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. Deno had raised a total of $26 million, including a Series A led by Sequoia.

articles.title: Ce signal a traversé 10 milliards d'années-lumière, et on a retrouvé son origine
articles.summary:
Lorsque l’on parle de distances dans l’espace lointain, tout paraît rapidement vertigineux.
Si l’unité astronomique, égale à la distance qui sépare la Terre du Soleil, peut être utile lorsque l’on reste dans les limites de notre Système solaire, il faut s’en séparer au moment d’aller plus loin et se mettre à compter en années-lumière. En une année, la lumière parcourt ainsi quasiment 10 000 milliards de kilomètres. Impossible à vraiment se représenter.
Sauf que le sursaut radio rapide (ou fast radio burst, FRB) étudié dans une étude publiée le 8 octobre nous pousse à nouveau à changer d’échelle.
Baptisé FRB 20240304B, ce signal ne dure que quelques millisecondes, et a été capté le 4 mars 2024. Comme pour tous les FRB, on ignore encore précisément ce qui le produit. La plupart de ces signaux ne se manifestent d’ailleurs qu’une seule fois. Mais celui-ci est particulier car c’est le plus lointain connu : sa lumière a voyagé un peu plus de 10 milliards d’années pour nous parvenir. Il a donc été émis alors que l’Univers n’était âgé « que » de trois milliards d’années environ.
Il y a 10 milliards d’années, dans une galaxie lointaine et jeune
FRB 20240304B fait l’objet d’une étude menée par l’astrophysicienne Manisha Caleb (université de Sydney) et parue dans la revue Science. Il a impliqué plusieurs télescopes à travers le monde, comme le radiotélescope MeerKAT en Afrique du Sud, mais aussi le télescope spatial James Webb. Sa caméra infrarouge a repéré la galaxie d’où est parti FRB…

articles.title: Por qué faltan diez días en el calendario de tu móvil si viajas hasta octubre de 1582
articles.summary:
Si abres el calendario de un iPhone y retrocedes más de cuatro siglos, vas a encontrarte con una curiosidad: del 4 de octubre de 1582 pasa al 15 de octubre. Esto solo te serviría si tuvieras un DeLorean y quisieras viajar a esa fecha concreta, aunque detrás de esos diez días que se evaporan sin dejar rastro hay una explicación. Apple es consciente de esa laguna temporal.
Once minutos y catorce segundos. Julio César instauró el calendario juliano en el año 45 a. C. Para ese calendario el año duraba 365,25 días. Y tenía un bisiesto cada cuatro años. Astronómicamente hablando, el año solar ronda los 365,2422 días. Esa diferencia de 11 minutos y 14 segundos al año generaba un día entero de desfase cada 130 años aproximadamente.
En el siglo XVI, el retraso acumulado por el calendario juliano era de diez días. No habría habido problemas de no ser por la religión: el Concilio de Nicea del año 325 fijó la Pascua tras el equinoccio de primavera del 21 de marzo. Para 1582, el equinoccio real se iba al 11 de marzo. De seguir acumulando desfase en el calendario, la Pascua corría el riesgo de terminar en verano.
Dormir el cuatro y despertar el quince. El papa Gregorio XIII promulgó en febrero de 1582 la bula Inter gravissimas. Para corregir unos doce siglos y medio de desviación astronómica, la Iglesia tomó una decisión: aparte de adoptar el nuevo calendario gregoriano, borró de este diez días. Desaparecieron.

As AI gobbles up an ever larger amount of energy, the hunt is on for efficient and cost-effective power sources. One of the companies leading the charge is Petra Power.
Petra, which was founded in 2017, sells solid oxide fuel cells — ceramic devices that convert fuel, like natural gas, into electric power without burning it. The company markets them as a more efficient and environmentally friendly way to operate data centers and large vehicles.

That heat creates motion. The motion powers an electromotive force, which eventually creates electricity. It’s a lot of steps, and they all have so much loss in them that you end up with a really inefficient system.”

Ce 7 octobre 2026, l’expert a appelé toute l’industrie à se préparer à passer en « mode bunker ». Dans un long billet publié sur X, il estime que l’intelligence artificielle pourrait venir casser la cryptographie qui protège Bitcoin, Ethereum, et les autres cryptos, dans un avenir proche… bien avant les tant redoutés ordinateurs quantiques.

 Today I call upon the blockchain industry to calmly begin planning for “bunker mode”. My personal recommendation is to set in motion a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses, i.e. addresses whose pubkeys remain hidden behind a hash.
Holders, starting with large and sophisticated ones, should consider moving the bulk of their funds to addresses that have never signed a transaction. And when they do sign one, they should also move remaining funds to a new address (possibly generated from the same seed phrase).
Don’t rush. While I believe there is cause for action a rushed migration would do more harm than good. Don’t panic either. Moving assets to protected addresses is a simple, preventative step which does not require new cryptography or new wallets.

But businesses should not be locked into a single machine
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is great at generating valuable insights, but what companies end up doing with those insights - that’s where true achievement lies, and that’s what companies should be focusing on.
This is one of the core messages delivered by Ryan Waite, Director of Open Source Ecosystems and Incubations at Microsoft, during his keynote, “From Open Source to Agentic Systems: Building the AI Native Era” at the Open Source Summit.
Waite described the interaction between AI and human expertise as a learning loop, a kind of hill-climbing machine that helps businesses improve, and keep on improving.
The knowledge belongs to the business
AI models are great at processing enormous amounts of information and generating insights at a scale humans cannot match (and sometimes cannot even fathom), but people bring something arguably more important to the table: context and judgement.
Putting insights into wider context, and using that to make conclusions, helps employees turn information into knowledge, and that knowledge later becomes part of the organization’s collective expertise. Saturday, October 10th 2026
AMD Reportedly Raises GDDR6 Prices for Board Partners
AMD has reportedly raised the price of the GDDR6 memory it supplies to its board partners, with the change said to be in effect since October 1. The claim comes from a post on the Chinese forum Board Channels, and it doesn't mention a percentage or a dollar figure. AMD sells its GPUs to add-in board (AIB) partners bundled with memory, so a costlier kit usually ends up in the retail price of the finished card. The timing matches the higher suggested Radeon prices in China reported earlier this week, where the RX 9070 went up by the equivalent of $104 and the RX 9060 XT 8 GB by $45, while the RX 9070 XT was left untouched.
NVIDIA, however, apparently hasn't sent its partners a similar notice for GDDR7 this time, and the same post suggests the company may not touch memory pricing again this year. That would be a small relief for GeForce buyers, although NVIDIA already raised GDDR6 and GDDR7 kit prices in July, and the RTX 5090 was tracked at 136% above MSRP globally in early September. AMD's partners have been through this a few times in 2026 already. A 10% hike on Radeon GPU kits was reported for July, and in September there was word of another 10% increase across GPUs, chipsets, and possibly CPUs, tied to rising TSMC wafer costs. AMD hasn't confirmed the latest increase, and we don't know how much or how soon store prices outside China will move.

articles.title: En 1971, Québec inundó 11.500 km² de bosque para crear un megaembalse y, sin saberlo, envenenó a un pueblo entero

Sin embargo, al crear embalses enormes en medio de la naturaleza salvaje, se desencadenó una bomba química silenciosa a consecuencia de la liberación del mercurio natural del suelo que envenenó el pescado del que dependía históricamente el pueblo indígena de los Cree.
Un gran problema. Un pescado que se saque de estas aguas a simple vista puede estar en perfecto estado y, sin embargo, ser un grave riesgo para el sistema nervioso de aquellas personas que decidan comerlo. Esta es la dura realidad con la que se topó el pueblo Cree tras la construcción de este gran complejo hidroeléctrico que alteró cinco ríos y la creación de inmensos embalses sumergieron más de 11.500 km2 de bosque boreal, un área comparable con la superficie de Qatar.
Pero la contaminación no fueron los generadores eléctricos ni la maquinaria pesada, sino el contacto de la propia agua con la tierra virgen.
El mercurio es una de esas toxinas de las que nos preocupamos mucho, sobre todo cuando vamos a tomar pescado. Pero en este caso el mercurio no provino de la contaminación industrial, sino que llevaba miles de años depositado en el suelo forestal. articles.title: Nikon le quitó el primer premio a un video científico por usar inteligencia artificial
articles.summary:
La empresa japonesa Nikon retiró el primer premio de su concurso de fotografía microscópica Small World in Motion después de confirmar que el video ganador había sido manipulado con inteligencia artificial, algo que las reglas del certamen prohíben expresamente.
El video, presentado por el investigador Ning Xu, mostraba lo que describía como estructuras parecidas a pelos que recubren las vías respiratorias moviéndose de forma irregular en un niño con discinesia ciliar primaria, una enfermedad respiratoria poco frecuente.
Nikon anunció la decisión el 9 de octubre a través de un comunicado publicado en su sitio oficial. “Tras reevaluar minuciosamente el video y el material adjunto, y consultar con miembros del jurado, determinamos que el video ganador no cumplía con las reglas del certamen sobre inteligencia artificial generativa”, informó la compañía.
El reglamento del concurso, vigente desde hace quince años, es explícito: “No se permiten videos generados por inteligencia artificial, y el organizador tiene derecho a solicitar el material original para su verificación”.
Las sospechas que empezaron en redes
El premio se había entregado un mes antes, pero científicos y ex jurados del certamen denunciaron en la red social LinkedIn que las estructuras celulares del video aparecían y desaparecían de un modo imposible en la biología real, según reportó la cadena BBC.

articles.title: El verdadero problema de las pantallas del móvil no es que nos deje ciegos, es que está alterando radicalmente nuestro sueño
articles.summary:
Son muchas las personas que, antes de ir a dormir, se meten en la cama y comienzan a hacer un poco de scroll con el móvil para ver las últimas tendencias de redes. Lo vendemos como una forma de "desconectar" antes de dormir, pero la realidad es que los oftalmólogos apuntan a que usar el teléfono móvil a oscuras con un brillo potente, puede hacer que la luz azul "impacte" de lleno en el ojo, provocando un daño acumulativo en la retina.
El verdadero problema. Más allá de este impacto, el daño más evidente de las pantallas está más relacionado con cómo usamos los ojos cuando las miramos. Aquí una revisión publicada en 2018 apunta a que la fatiga visual digital afecta al 50% o más de los usuarios de ordenadores, y los síntomas se dividen en problemas acomodativos por el esfuerzo que le estamos obligando a hacer al cristalino, y la sequedad ocular.
Y esta sequedad ocular tiene mucho sentido, porque un ser humano normal parpadea unas 15 veces por minuto, pero cuando fijamos la vista en una pantalla, esa frecuencia puede reducirse a la mitad. Lo que provoca esto es que existe una menor lubricación y, por tanto, ojo seco.
Presión intraocular. Este es un efecto medible e importante, puesto que en un estudio con 39 jóvenes demostró que utilizar un smartphone con luz tenue elevó la presión intraocular un 24,7% a los 15 minutos, frente a una subida del 12,9% con luz diurna. Aunque la buena noticia es que la presión vuelve a la normalidad tras dejar el móvil.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved.
In a Saturday morning post on X, Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
“We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI.
As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”
“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said. “Think of it like an emergency brake.”
Nadella’s comments come as leading AI companies acknowledge more and more incidents where they seemed to lose control of their models, and after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan for more cautious AI development.

"Confiar en los modelos lo menos posible". Satya Nadella ha hablado en Twitter y ha apostado por atar a la inteligencia artificial en corto: separar el suministro de inteligencia de la autoridad sobre ella. O lo que es lo mismo, rodear a los modelos de reglas, permisos y vigilancia independiente. La idea de base es simple: con el software tradicional podíamos rastrear un comportamiento hasta una línea de código, pero con los modelos actuales no.
Mucho poder y poca explicación. Las empresas están poniendo agentes de IA a trabajar en sistemas importantes, con acceso a datos sensibles y confidenciales pese a que no sabemos explicar por qué un modelo de IA avanzado hace lo que hace. Es más, incluso a actuar en nuestro nombre. Por eso Nadella es tajante: “No podemos externalizar la responsabilidad de lo que la inteligencia hace en nuestro nombre”. Y añade que las garantías del proveedor del modelo no nos eximen de esa responsabilidad.
Tratar a la IA como un riesgo interno. Lo que propone es tratar a los modelos como a un empleado con muchos permisos: la menor autoridad posible, registro de todo lo que hacen y capacidad para pararlos. No lo plantea porque sean necesariamente maliciosos, sino porque cualquier actor capaz con acceso a sistemas importantes puede equivocarse o ser comprometido.

articles.title: Does a VPN protect your privacy when using ChatGPT or Claude?
articles.summary:
Does a VPN protect your privacy when using ChatGPT or Claude? What network encryption can and can’t hide from AI
A VPN is great at hiding where you are and what your internet provider sees. However, when you’re chatting with ChatGPT or Claude, your privacy depends on something far more complicated than a tunnel through the internet.
Even the best VPNs won’t stop AI companies from reading, storing, and learning from everything you type. In this article, we’ll unpack exactly what data these platforms see, why encryption has limits, and what you can actually do to protect yourself.
What chatbots see (and what a VPN actually hides)
Without a VPN, OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Anthropic (Claude) can typically see a lot about your connection. Your IP address reveals your approximate geographic location. Device metadata follows alongside that, including your browser type, operating system, and unique device identifiers.
According to OpenAI’s privacy policy, the company collects your IP address; device information, including unique identifiers; cookie data; and your location, along with your email address and payment information.
Anthropic does the same. Their policy covers location, connection details, and device usage patterns, especially on the mobile app. Different wording, same result: both companies can see roughly where you are and what you’re using to talk to them.

articles.summary:
New Cray-1 supercomputer replica built with 30 vintage Mac Minis and packs 1.5 TFLOPS of compute — passively cooled tribute is 9,375x faster than the 1976 supercomputer
The original may be weak by today's standards, but it did an awesome job of improving many people's lives.
Spain’s Museo de Historia de la Computación unveiled its 18-month-long project to commemorate the 50th anniversary of both the Cray-1’s first operational use in Los Alamos and Apple’s founding. The replica uses 30 Mac Minis, 25 dual-core i5 units, and five quad-core i7 units from 2012-2014, totaling 70 cores that produce a peak of 1.5 TeraFLOPS; a theoretical 9,375x jump from the original Cray-1's 160 MegaFLOPS. After one quad-core machine went offline, the current reported peak sits at 1.3 TeraFLOPS.
The original Cray-1 is considered to be the first commercially successful supercomputer, with 80 systems sold in its heyday. Science and engineering institutions sought it out to churn through gigantic datasets for uses ranging from intense weather prediction and aerodynamics to nuclear physics and structural analysis, among many others.
It was very efficient at these computations thanks to vector processing, a computing technique we take for granted nowadays. Vector computing made this supercomputer so powerful; while most computers still handled tasks one instruction at a time, the Cray-1 could process chunks of numbers in parallel, saving a huge amount of time.

Ni l’un ni l’autre ne confirme une intrusion dans les serveurs de l’école, et tous deux cherchent encore à comprendre comment un seul pirate a pu ouvrir autant de fiches en si peu de temps. Wie Neowin berichtet, soll es sich bei der neuen Navigationshilfe für den Datei-Explorer um das aus Linux- und Unix-Umgebungen bekannte Tilde-Symbol (~) handeln. Die Eingabe der Tilde in der Adressleiste des Datei-Explorers bringt die Nutzer:innen künftig direkt in den Benutzerordner ihres Profils.

Deux câbles de 2 m, une puissance de charge annoncée jusqu’à 240 W et une gaine tressée : ce lot INIU convient aux appareils équipés d’un port USB-C.
Amazon affiche le lot de deux câbles USB-C vers USB-C INIU de 2 m à 10,28 €, contre un ancien prix indiqué de 11,99 €. Cela représente une économie de 1,71 €, soit environ 14 %. Chaque câble revient ainsi à 5,14 €. L’offre concerne la version noire avec indicateur LED, expédiée par Amazon.
Jusqu’à 240 W pour la recharge des appareils compatibles
Ces câbles disposent d’un connecteur USB-C à chaque extrémité et acceptent une puissance de charge annoncée jusqu’à 240 W. Ils peuvent servir à alimenter un ordinateur portable, une tablette, un smartphone ou une console portable compatible. Cette valeur constitue toutefois un plafond : la puissance réellement délivrée dépend du chargeur et de l’appareil raccordé. Un téléphone ne recevra donc pas automatiquement 240 W.
Leur longueur de 2 m chacun laisse davantage de liberté qu’un câble court pour utiliser un appareil pendant sa recharge. Le lot permet, par exemple, de conserver un câble sur le bureau et un second dans un sac. Aucun adaptateur secteur n’est compris dans cette offre.

El último en sumarse ha sido Meta, que hace un mes presentó Muse, un agente que lee tu correo, gestiona tu calendario, rellena formularios y compra en tu nombre.
Por qué es importante. El agente personal es la gran apuesta tras la era del chatbot. Su valor depende directamente de cuánto acceso le das. Por eso la privacidad esta vez no es un fallo que se pueda corregir. Es el precio de entrada.

articles.title: Security-Fragebögen: Compliance einmal aufbauen, oft nutzen
articles.summary:
Einmal dokumentieren, überall nachweisen: So skaliert Compliance mit deinen Enterprise-Kunden
Und der Fragebogen ist erst der Anfang: Der nächste Kunde verlangt ISO 27001, ein Automotive-Kunde TISAX, ein US-Kunde SOC 2. Je größer die Kunden werden, desto mehr entscheiden schnelle und belastbare Compliance-Nachweise über den Vertriebserfolg.
Was Enterprise-Kunden wirklich prüfen
Security-Fragebögen sehen auf den ersten Blick nach vielen unterschiedlichen Anforderungen aus, drehen sich inhaltlich jedoch meist um dieselben Fragen:
- Wer darf auf welche Systeme zugreifen (Berechtigungskonzept)?
- Welche Dienstleister verarbeiten Daten (Vendor Management)?
- Wie werden Sicherheitsvorfälle behandelt und welche Löschfristen gelten?
- Welche technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen (TOMs) sind konkret umgesetzt?
Bei kleineren Deals reicht oft eine Selbstauskunft. Bei Enterprise-Kunden, regulatorischen Vorgaben (wie NIS2, DORA, dem Cyber Resilience Act oder dem EU AI Act) und branchenspezifischen Standards kommen formale Nachweise wie ISO 27001, SOC 2 oder TISAX hinzu.
Der Kunde fragt dabei nach der Kontrolle und dem Nachweis, nicht nach dem spezifischen Framework dahinter. Viele Unternehmen haben deshalb kein neues Compliance-Problem, sondern ein Wiederverwendungsproblem: Wer jedes Framework als separates Projekt behandelt, beschreibt Controls neu, sucht Nachweise erneut zusammen und dokumentiert Verantwortlichkeiten mehrfach.

articles.title: Nachteulen im 9-to-5-Job: Warum starre Arbeitszeiten krank machen
articles.summary:
Studie belegt: Warum Nachteulen im 9-to-5-Job früher krank werden
Menschen mit einer späten inneren Uhr haben ein um rund 70 Prozent höheres Risiko, vorzeitig aus dem Erwerbsleben auszuscheiden. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt ein Team von Forscher:innen der finnischen Universität Oulu, wie in einer im Fachjournal Occupational and Environmental Medicine veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.
Die Mediziner:innen analysierten die Daten von 5.679 Teilnehmer:innen einer finnischen Geburtskohorte aus dem Jahr 1966. Die Beobachtung erstreckte sich über einen Zeitraum von zwölf Jahren, in dem das Lebensalter der Personen von 46 auf 57 Jahre anstieg.
Dabei zeigte sich, dass sogenannte Nachteulen deutlich häufiger eine Erwerbsminderungsrente in Anspruch nehmen mussten als Morgentypen (Lerchen) oder keine den beiden Extremen zuzuordnende Personen. Dieser Unterschied blieb bei beiden Geschlechtern als konstante statistische Größe bestehen, selbst als externe Faktoren wie Bildungsebene, Einkommen und der spezifische Beruf herausgerechnet wurden.
Wenn die innere Uhr gegen den Wecker arbeitet
Die Zuordnung zu den jeweiligen Biorhythmen erfolgte nicht allein auf Basis subjektiver Einschätzungen der Proband:innen. Das Team der Universität Oulu nutzte validierte Fragebögen, die detailliert erfassten, wie schwer das Aufwachen fiel und wie stark die Müdigkeit in der ersten halben Stunde des Tages ausgeprägt war.

The newly formed Consumer Fairness and Public Protection Division is also targeting Roblox and AppLovin.
California is taking another swing at banning 3D-printed “ghost guns,” and this time the target is one of the world’s largest manufacturers of 3D printing filament. Polymaker LLC, headquartered in Shanghai with U.S. operations based in Houston, was named in a civil lawsuit filed October 5, 2026, by San Diego County Counsel on behalf of the People of the State of California. The complaint alleges that Polymaker marketed its filament in such a way as to appeal to gun enthusiasts and thus transform harmless PLA into a regulated “firearm precursor part.”
Under California law, a firearm precursor part is “defined to include any article marketed or sold to the public to become or be used as the frame or receiver of a functional firearm once completed, assembled or converted,” according to the civil complaint filed in San Diego County Superior Court. The County seeks disgorgement of profits, civil penalties and injunctive relief.

articles.title: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
articles.summary:
For about a decade, the mainstream understanding has been that psychedelics cause chaos in the brain. Brain networks—the stable patterns of communication that handle vision, attention, or our sense of self, and more—loosen and start talking to each other all at once. EEG traces get noisier and more complex. “Think of the networks of the brain as highways,” says Devon Stoliker, a neuroscientist at Monash University. “Under psychedelics, these highways break down into many different directions.”
In a recent Nature study, Stoliker’s team designed an experiment to test whether these directions are truly chaotic and random. Researchers gathered 62 people who had never taken a psychedelic before, gave them 19 milligrams of psilocybin, a common psychedelic found in certain fungi, and scanned their brains. Then, they used AI to analyze the drugged and sober brain scans. What emerged was not exactly chaos.
An uninterrupted trip
Stoliker thinks chaos is not a satisfactory explanation for psychedelics’ effect on the brain. “It never really explained why an individual would have a meaningful experience, why they might have insight, why they might experience clarity, and why these might translate into positive psychological changes,” Stoliker says. To investigate if there are other explanations, he and his colleagues designed a study called PsiConnect.
